text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Wednesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- There is no alternative to Lithuania's membership to NATO, Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas told the OSCE summit in Lisbon.
- Latvia is looking for ways to continue negotiations with the new Lithuanian government, state secretary of the Latvian Foreign Ministry Maris Riekstinsh said.
- Parliament has decided to carry out an independent audit of state loans and obligations made before December 1, 1996.
- The Centre Union is to get two posts in the new cabinet of ministers.
- The Canadian federal royal corporation Atomic Energy of Canada are sure that Lithuania suffers huge loses buying vats to store waste nuclear fuel from the German GNB company.
- Refinery Mazeikiu Nafta fears the return to power of Gediminas Vagnorius as he wants to revise the law on forming a national oil company.

- The director of the policy department of the Bank of Lithuania Gitanas Nauseda told the Confederation of Industrialists about the intended changes in monetary politics. The central bank intends to scrap the currency board and peg the litas to both the German mark and the dollar.
- The assets of state owned and joint stock companies were estimated 39.4 billion litas during first half of 1996, Statistics Department data reveals.
- In October as well as in September the inflation rate in Lithuania was the lowest among the three Baltic countries at 0.1 percent in Lithuania, 1.2 percent in Latvia and 0.6 percent in Estonia.

- The minimum salary in Lithuania is $75, in Latvia $68.8 and in Estonia $55.6. The average salary in October was $176 in Lithuania, $200 in Latvia and $246 in Estonia. The average pension during the third quarter of 1996 was $49 in Lithuania, $70 in Latvia and $80 in Estonia.
